type: Power Stack LNG + fertilizer stock research overlay
evidencePolicy: Primary/company and high-quality current reporting first. Creator/social material remains hypothesis-only. Theme strength changes research priority and margin-of-safety requirements, not company fundamental scores. Do not chase war-gap moves.

executiveJudgement.lng: KEEP FIRST-CLASS / DEEPEN STOCK LADDER. Global LNG rerouting is already a top-five Power Stack theme. The current Hormuz constraint, low European storage and durable gas-fired power/import infrastructure growth strengthen the strategic value of non-Hormuz LNG capacity and contracted US gas infrastructure. Prefer contracted operating cash flow over spot-only beta or financing-heavy greenfield optionality.
executiveJudgement.fertilizer: KEEP ACTIVE / SPLIT BY NUTRIENT AND FEEDSTOCK. The spring urea spike already mean-reverted toward pre-conflict levels, proving that headline scarcity cannot be extrapolated. Renewed Hormuz stress creates re-shock optionality in nitrogen, while sulfur/phosphate economics remain a separate margin problem. CF, NTR and MOS should not be modeled as interchangeable fertilizer exposures.

energy-security-rerouting.decision: NO DUPLICATE THEME; deepen existing LNG/global-gas rerouting theme
transmission: Hormuz/Qatar LNG disruption -> Europe and Asia compete for Atlantic LNG -> TTF/JKM and electricity inflation
Higher LNG prices -> stronger utilization/contracting economics for US LNG exporters and Gulf Coast gas infrastructure
US gas supply remains comparatively abundant -> Henry Hub can stay soft even while global LNG scarcity raises exporter margins and strategic value
Gas-fired generation and LNG infrastructure buildout extend the theme beyond the current war shock
energy-security-rerouting.confirmation: Persistently low Gulf LNG loadings/transits, low EU storage, high TTF/JKM, strong US LNG feedgas/utilization, new long-term contracts and infrastructure awards.
energy-security-rerouting.invalidation: Durable Gulf normalization, rapid EU storage recovery, collapsing Atlantic-basin spreads and weakening long-term contracting/utilization.

fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.decision: KEEP ACTIVE; rewrite as nutrient/feedstock divergence rather than blanket fertilizer scarcity
transmission: Middle East nitrogen disruption and shipping risk support ammonia/urea scarcity optionality
Cheap North American gas versus Europe/Asia improves relative nitrogen economics for CF/NTR
Farmer affordability and seasonal demand cap pass-through and create violent mean reversion
Sulfur scarcity raises phosphate production costs, so a fertilizer supply shock can hurt MOS phosphate margins even while finished phosphate prices rise
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.confirmation: Urea/ammonia re-tighten with sustained export/logistics constraints while North American gas remains advantaged; potash demand/affordability remains constructive; sulfur costs stop worsening for phosphate producers.
fertilizer-feedstock-divergence.invalidation: Middle East nitrogen capacity/exports normalize, China export supply expands, grain/farm economics weaken materially, or North American gas loses its feedstock advantage.

stockLadder.name: Cheniere Energy
stockLadder.why: Best blend of operating scale, contract visibility, cash generation and incremental capacity. Q2 revenue was $5.73B, adjusted EBITDA $1.80B and DCF $1.17B; 184 cargoes were exported and 2026 production guidance tightened to 53-54 mtpa.
stockLadder.risk: Rapid normalization of global LNG scarcity, execution/financing risk on expansions, or valuation becoming too stretched.
stockLadder.action: Retain existing retest discipline; do not convert a strategic thesis into a spot-gas momentum chase.

stockLadder.name: Baker Hughes
stockLadder.why: Picks-and-shovels exposure to LNG liquefaction, gas turbines and thermal management offers a less commodity-directional expression of the buildout.
stockLadder.risk: Integration/leverage after Chart Industries acquisition and slowdown in LNG equipment orders.

stockLadder.name: Williams Companies
stockLadder.theme: US gas infrastructure / Haynesville-to-Gulf Coast LNG
stockLadder.why: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $1.921B, AFFO $1.450B and dividend coverage 2.26x. Momentum adds 4,000+ miles of pipe, 6 Bcf/d gathering and 4.05 Bcf/d take-or-pay transport capacity tied to Haynesville LNG/power demand.
stockLadder.risk: NESE permitting setback plus recent debt issuance/capital intensity keep the hurdle higher.
stockLadder.promotionTrigger: Permitting risk becomes bounded while Momentum integration, contracted volumes and AFFO conversion remain on plan.

stockLadder.name: EQT Corporation
stockLadder.stance: STRUCTURAL LNG OPTIONALITY, NOT DIRECT LNG SPREAD
stockLadder.why: Q2 execution was strong and the company signed a five-year 0.5 mtpa LNG offtake starting in 2028, expected to add about $45M of 2028 FCF at then-current strip pricing.
stockLadder.risk: US gas oversupply can keep Henry Hub soft; upstream gas beta is less protected than liquefaction/infrastructure cash flow.
stockLadder.promotionTrigger: Tighter US gas balances plus durable FCF and larger LNG-linked contracting without sacrificing capital discipline.

stockLadder.name: Venture Global
stockLadder.why: Q2 revenue rose to $4.6B, adjusted EBITDA to $2.5B and 127 cargoes were exported; 2026 EBITDA guidance increased to $8.7-9.1B and CP2 remains on schedule for first LNG in H2 2027.
stockLadder.risk: Large capex/financing burden, project execution and substantial rerating after a very strong 2026 share-price move.
stockLadder.promotionTrigger: Price/valuation reset plus financing and CP2 milestones that preserve per-share cash-flow economics.

stockLadder.name: Golar LNG
stockLadder.why: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $127M and Hilli completed its Cameroon contract with 100% economic uptime before a new 20-year contract from 2027. A fourth 3.5 mtpa FLNG unit targets end-2029 delivery.
stockLadder.risk: Contractual debt was about $2.68B and the new FLNG project costs about $2.45B, making rates, project finance and execution first-order risks.
stockLadder.promotionTrigger: Project financing/contract backstop materially de-risks the fourth FLNG without weakening balance-sheet resilience.

stockLadder.name: CF Industries
stockLadder.why: CF estimates the conflict removed roughly 4.0-4.5Mt of traded urea and ~1Mt of ammonia from Middle East supply to date, while North American gas remains a structural cost advantage. But Q2 also proved prices can fall back rapidly when seasonal demand softens and supply-return expectations rise.
stockLadder.risk: Urea normalization, farmer affordability, China exports, and loss of cheap-gas advantage.
stockLadder.action: Treat renewed Hormuz stress as re-shock optionality, not evidence that the spring price spike is permanent.

stockLadder.name: Nutrien
stockLadder.why: Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $2.43B. Nutrien reported record first-half potash volumes, constructive potash affordability and a 74-77Mt 2026 global shipment outlook, while nitrogen benefits from trade disruption and energy-cost divergence.
stockLadder.risk: Farm credit/affordability, potash deferral, and less upside convexity than CF in a nitrogen shock.
stockLadder.action: Use as the more diversified, lower-beta agriculture input expression.

stockLadder.name: The Mosaic Company
stockLadder.why: Potash exposure benefits from constructive global demand, but phosphate economics are being squeezed by sulfur availability and cost. The same Middle East disruption that lifts fertilizer scarcity can raise Mosaic's input bill.
stockLadder.risk: Persistently elevated sulfur/ammonia costs, phosphate curtailments and weak margin conversion.
stockLadder.promotionTrigger: Sulfur costs normalize or finished-phosphate pricing demonstrably outruns raw-material inflation while potash stays firm.

portfolioImplication: Do not add broad fertilizer or LNG beta mechanically. Current hierarchy is LNG > BKR > WMB/EQT/VG research > GLNG satellite on gas/LNG; CF > NTR > MOS conditional on fertilizer. This preserves Power Stack's preference for contracted/operating cash flow under restrictive long-end yields.
